headline: ESMA Sets CSRD Priorities; Green Claims Enforcement Intensifies Across EU
summary: ESMA has outlined enforcement priorities for CSRD disclosures as national regulators urge listed firms to prepare. Green claims face heightened scrutiny following new ESMA guidance and European Commission action. Meanwhile, EU trilogue negotiations have commenced regarding potential CBAM scope extensions.

items.title: ESMA sets enforcement priorities for upcoming CSRD reporting
items.what: ESMA established reporting enforcement priorities focusing on double materiality, impacts, risks, opportunities, and targets. Spanish regulators simultaneously urged listed companies with over 1,000 employees to align disclosures with CSRD.
items.meaning: As a listed company with over 1,000 employees, CSRD applies to your FY2027 reporting. Regulators will scrutinise your Chinese supplier data, target setting, and materiality assessments.
items.action: Ensure your supplier sustainability data collection aligns with ESMA's double materiality and target verification priorities.

sources.title: ESMA to Focus on Materiality, Impacts, Risks, Opportunities and Targets as Sustainability Reporting Enforcement Priorities
The CNMV urges listed companies with more than 1,000 employees to align their sustainability reports with the CSRD.

items.title: Increased scrutiny and guidance on EU green claims
items.what: ESMA issued guidance on climate transition claims, while the European Commission secured commitments from major consumer brands to correct misleading recycling claims.
items.meaning: Marketing claims regarding tool packaging, battery recyclability, or climate impacts face immediate supervisory enforcement and strict substantiation requirements across EU markets.
items.action: Audit product packaging and marketing claims against ESMA guidance to prevent regulatory intervention.

sources.title: ESMA Guidance on Impact and Climate Transition Claims
EU Commission secures recycling claim changes from Coca-Cola, Nestlé and Danone

items.title: Trilogues begin on potential CBAM scope extension
items.what: EU trilogue negotiations have commenced on CBAM, with industry groups advocating for a broader product scope. Separately, UK HMRC issued guidance on UK CBAM launching in 2027.
items.meaning: Finished power tools currently fall outside basic metal CBAM tariffs, but scope expansion could affect downstream hardware products or UK sales.
items.action: Track trilogue proposals to assess whether downstream finished goods might eventually enter scope.

sources.title: Industries urge ‘broadest possible’ CBAM extension, trilogues begin
UK CBAM from 1 January 2027: HMRC guidance explained

items.title: EFRAG consults on 2027–2029 sustainability agenda
items.what: EFRAG launched a public consultation regarding its work programme for 2027–2029 under the CSRD framework.
items.meaning: The consultation will shape future sector-specific ESRS standards and long-term supply chain disclosure expectations.
items.action: Monitor EFRAG outputs to anticipate future reporting requirements for tool manufacturing.

sources.title: EU CSRD: EFRAG launched consultation on its 2027–2029 sustainability reporting agenda, Julia Voskoboinikova
